text:
alana_finance: Heads-up — invoice 2026-03-01 (acct RW-789) shows a $12.3k overage on Dedicated (eu-west-2-prod). Can someone reconcile reserved commits vs burst charges?

raj_billing: Looking now. Quick Q: are we counting burst GPU-hours under 'overage' or under a separate 'burst' line? I see both on the invoice. :thinking:

jiro_infra: We emit a 'burst' tag when autoscaler spins extra nodes beyond reserved pool. Those should be billed at burst rate, not overage, but the invoice mapper might fold them into overage if commit mapping fails.

mia_acct: Customer is asking why they hit overage even though they had a 50-GPU reserved commit for March. They used occasional spikes but average was < commit.

raj_billing: Can you paste the invoice fragment? I'll scan for commit IDs and pool names.

jiro_infra: Sure — snippet from our usage export:`
```
pool_name,commit_id,timestamp,gpu_hours,tag
eu-west-2-prod,COMMIT-50G-2026-03,2026-03-12T03:11:00Z,2,reserved
eu-west-2-prod,COMMIT-50G-2026-03,2026-03-12T03:12:00Z,4,burst
eu-west-2-prod,,2026-03-12T03:13:00Z,1,burst
```

alana_finance: Invoice lines look like this:`
```
Line 1123: Dedicated reserved commit COMMIT-50G-2026-03 - $50,000
Line 1124: Dedicated overage (eu-west-2-prod) - $12,300
Line 1125: Burst usage surcharge - $0.00
```

raj_billing: Ah — invoice shows Burst usage surcharge $0.00 but overage nonzero. That suggests the billing pipeline failed to map some burst-tagged rows to the burst surcharge bucket and instead attributed to generic overage. I'll run the mapper job against the export now.

billing-bot: Started job billing-mapper-run-1712002501 for account RW-789. ETA ~2m.

raj_billing: Mapper log: `ERROR: missing_commit_id for rows with burst tag` — seems there are rows missing commit_id because of a telemetry race during node termination. I'll patch the join to fall back to pool_name->commit table.

jiro_infra: Patch sounds good. Also note: we throttle allowed burst for reserved pools to 25% of commit; any excess should be counted as overage. Double-check the usage windows — customer had one 4-hour spike that exceeded that limit.

mia_acct: Customer also asked about SLA credits. They claim latency SLO downtime on 2026-03-12 for ~3 hours. How are SLA credits computed vs our committed monthly fee?

alana_finance: Our SLA policy: credit = min(10% of monthly committed fee, proportional to minutes of breach). For 3hrs on a monthly commit of $50k, credit = 10% * $50k * (180 / total_month_minutes). But we usually calculate pro rata of the 10% cap. I'll run exact calc if the ops incident is confirmed.

raj_billing: Mapper run complete. Result: $9,800 of the $12.3k was incorrectly bucketed — should be 'burst surcharge'. Updated invoice draft attached to portal (link sent to finance inbox). Remaining $2.5k is true overage because burst exceeded 25% threshold.

alana_finance: Good. Action items: 1) reissue corrected invoice to customer with note about invoice map bug and corrected lines; 2) apply SLA credit draft once infra confirms incident; 3) engineering to add fallback in telemetry join to avoid missing commit_id.

jiro_infra: I'll open a PR for the fallback and add a short-term alert when commit_id is null for burst rows. ETA end of day.

mia_acct: I'll draft the customer message: apologize, explain corrected line items (showing reserved vs burst vs overage), include provisional SLA credit calc, and offer a 30% discount on next month reserved commit as a gesture. Will share for review.

alana_finance: Perfect. tagging @raj_billing and @jiro_infra for follow-ups. Thanks — will wait for the corrected invoice before issuing final credit. :thumbsup:
